title: Half-density Hellinger bridge for the theta-half Kubo--Mori shell
question: Can the absolute theta-half Kubo--Mori shell be factored through the commutator and anticommutator of the Gibbs half-density, yielding a two-sided GNS/Hellinger bound that makes the square-root locality debt explicit?
method: Use the actual-Q3 edge and square finite fixtures from R-371/R-373 with all translated sites and bond terms, both term orders, both time signs, every prefix position and both history adjoints.
Diagonalize the doubled bond generator, construct the normalized Gibbs weights p_i and the half-density R=diag(sqrt(p_i)), and center every moved Hermitian witness.
Evaluate the theta-half shell, the Frobenius squares of [R,X] and {R,X}, the pair factorization, the geometric Cauchy envelope and the arithmetic envelope recovering 4 Tr(rho X^2).
Reconstruct the same grid without importing the primary audit and compile the scalar factorization/arithmetic envelope in Lean R378.
finding: The primary lane passes 25454/25454 assertions and the non-importing independent lane passes 8/8 aggregate assertions over 2816 all-prefix contexts. The integrated verifier passes 68/68 and Lean R378 compiles. The maximum shell is 1.4610968881346746, the maximum geometric half-density bound is 18.402415064535205, and the maximum recovered arithmetic bound is 166.59306606647507. The largest shell/geometric-bound ratio is 0.5380346350964185 and the largest shell/arithmetic ratio is 0.008770454393051757. Primary and independent values agree within 1.137e-12.
decision_reason: The half-density factorization exposes the R-377 square-root debt as two positive, orientation-aware GNS legs. It is a genuinely different interface from the R-373 scalar cap and R-371 arithmetic second-moment reduction, and the finite data show a much smaller geometric envelope than the recovered arithmetic envelope. The finite proxy does not establish either leg uniformly, so no common-alpha or QFT promotion is made.

adversarial_review.check: The pair identity is evaluated with absolute probability differences and nonnegative square roots; no energy ordering is assumed.
The shell is bounded by Cauchy on two nonnegative spectral rows; the geometric mean is not treated as an equality.
The commutator and anticommutator are formed as actual products with the same half-density on both sides; no commutation through X is used.
The moved witness is symmetrized before both legs are formed, and anti-Hermitian/Hermitian residuals are checked.
Zero transition gaps remain in the sums and no division by an energy difference occurs.
The sum of the two half-density squares is compared with 4 Tr(rho X^2) in the bond eigenbasis rather than inferred from a commuting model.
The anticommutator cost grows on the finite edge sweep from d=3 to d=6, so uniformity is not silently claimed.
The Gibbs matrix is the finite doubled-bond proxy, not a thermodynamic KMS state or OS reconstruction.
The independent lane rebuilds the oscillator, graph, Gibbs spectrum, prefixes and half-density products without importing the primary audit.
The finite bridge does not prove modular tails, a common core, common alpha, KMS/GNS dynamics, a gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A.

next_action: Prove a source-, volume- and cutoff-uniform estimate for both half-density legs on one Hamiltonian-derived core, then insert their geometric mean into the R-377 odd-resolvent telescope for direct D and delta-D orientations.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite half-density/GNS interface only. It does not prove operator-norm locality, modular tails, common core, common alpha, KMS/GNS dynamics, a gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A.
no_overclaim: R-378 separates the finite square-root debt into two computable positive legs; finite improvement is not a uniform theorem or a QFT closure.
